title: Carrier jet
idea: A seventies navy carrier jet, worked on by its deck crew: every marking does a job, every part is made of what a jet's part is made of, and the car has lived on a carrier.
words: hangar; the moodboard's B, carrier jet (2026-10-07)
ground_rules: Each detail sits where a navy jet has it, for that job: a few at a time, never spread over the car by a rule.
Three distances: what reads from far (the colours), from the chase camera (the markings), and close up in the garage (the small things).
Words: a few small stencils, as a jet carries them (the user, 2026-10-07: "Sure" to small words): the identity's type, on flat rooms only, in a step of their own. No other words.

areas.about: What reads from far, and the quiet second layer that keeps the big grey and white areas from looking flat.

items.why: A navy jet's two colours, split along the model's own lines.
Corrosion touch-ups in a fresher grey on a few whole panels, one side more than the other: tone on tone, never flat.
items.how: meshlines.panel on 3 or 4 panels, not mirrored, touch-up grey satin

items.why: Salt and hydraulic grime, faint on top, heavier low and behind the wheels.
items.how: WE-06 greasy, light, low on the body and behind each wheel

items.what: A hard line where the colours meet
items.why: A navy jet's split is masked, crisp: the one hard edge; heat and grime fade softly.

areas.about: The radar, the probe and the glare shield ahead of the pilot.

items.why: The radar's cone is flat black on a seventies navy jet: the nose tip as its own object.
items.how: the nose tip, matte radome black

items.why: A flat dark panel ahead of the cockpit, so the sun doesn't dazzle the pilot.
items.how: the nose's top from the cockpit's front (z 90) to clear of the nose fin's plate (z 115), between the nose's rolled edges, matte

items.why: The pale green strips a wingman flies on at night, one on each side of the nose.
items.how: a 2.5 cm strip along one of the model's lines on the nose's side, about 20 cm long, formation green

items.why: The nose's air-data probe: bare metal, its tip red.
items.how: the nose sensor, polished, a red tip

items.why: The radar bay's access door: one outline, a fastener at each corner.
items.how: one rounded box outline on the nose's side, 0.4 cm black, four small dots

areas.about: Where the crew helps the pilot in and out.

items.why: The ejection seat's danger triangle, red in white.
The arrow a rescuer follows to the canopy release: one each side.
items.how: a small arrow mark on the cockpit surround's side, pointing at the opening, yellow on a red edge

items.why: The seat's yellow-and-black striped pull handle.
items.how: a small striped zone on the seat's front

items.why: The pilot's harness in olive webbing, its buckles bare metal.
items.how: seat belt webbing olive; belt buckle polished

items.why: The squadron's badge on each rear quarter panel, the flap by the cockpit's back, where the chase camera sees it.
items.how: marks on the rear quarter panel's calm room, about 14 cm: blue disc, gold ring, gold bolt

items.why: Beside the rescue arrow.
items.how: a placard or text, 2 cm, red, beside the arrow

areas.about: The air intakes and the wing roots the crew climbs over.

items.why: The danger edge round each intake.
Pointing into the intake: keep clear.
Where it's safe to step, on the wing root.
The walkway's rough dark grip, so boots don't slip on a wet deck.
items.how: fill the walkway outline, textured wrap non-skid

items.why: Two footholds up the sidepod's side to the walkway.
items.how: two small box outlines, 4 by 3 cm, on the sidepod's flank below the walkway

items.why: NO STEP just outside the walkway; DANGER beside the intake's chevrons.
items.how: text 2 to 2.5 cm, black and red, on flat rooms

areas.about: What the driving camera sees: the spine, the exhausts and the hook.

items.why: The squadron's blue along each rear flank, its lower edge a gold pinstripe: the colour you see from the chase camera.
items.how: a band beside the line along the rear flank's top, from the sidepod's back corner towards the tail; a gold pinstripe on its lower edge

items.why: The panels round the exhausts in bare titanium, fading into the grey: the one soft colour change.
items.how: the tail corners and the tail panel, brushed titanium, a fade into the gull grey ahead of them

items.why: A carrier jet's hook in black and white bands: the carrier's signature.
items.how: bands across the diffuser's middle strake or the rear undertray, black and white

items.why: The car's own fuel cap as the jet's gravity filler: steel, a red ring round it.
items.how: the fuel cap polished, a red ring on the deck round it

items.why: The red light on the spine.
items.how: the antenna red, glowing at night

items.why: The engine bay's door on the rear flank: one outline, its fasteners.
items.how: one outline with corner dots on each rear flank's calm room

areas.about: The undercarriage, built to be slammed onto a deck.

items.why: A gear door's red danger edge.
The shock struts' polished legs.
A white bar across tyre and rim, to see if the tyre has crept.
items.how: a short white bar across the tyre's shoulder and the cover's red rim, one per wheel

items.why: Dark heat-worn metal behind the wheels.
items.how: brake caliper gunmetal

items.why: The emblem's bolt in gold on each wheel cover's hub.
items.how: a small gold bolt mark on the wheel cover hub

areas.about: Under and inside: wheel wells, the wing, the intakes' insides.

items.why: A navy jet's undercarriage bays are gloss white.
The front wing's leading edge polished, as a jet's wing edges are.
items.how: a strip along the front wing's front edge, polished aluminium

items.why: The intakes' wire screens in dull steel against the white.
items.how: sidepod grille, brushed steel

items.why: The wheel rings and speed numbers in the strips' pale green.
The rear and brake lights in insignia red.

identity.about: What a livery designer is handed before the first line: an invented squadron's own pieces, each used at more than one size.
identity.squadron: An invented navy fighter squadron, blue and gold. Its name is never written on the car.

emblem.what: A gold lightning bolt on a squadron-blue disc, in a thin gold ring

motif.why: A broad squadron-blue band, its edge a gold pinstripe, as squadron colours run along a jet's fuselage.
The emblem's bolt alone, gold, a signature on small parts.

type.how: Black Ops One (a stencil face), capitals 2 to 3 cm high; black on the grey or white, red where it warns. Only NO STEP, RESCUE and DANGER.

texture.how: A few panels in fresher touch-up grey, satin against the old semi-gloss; carrier grime low and behind the wheels. Tone on tone, never a pattern.

lines.how: Only where the jet has them: the colour split, the walkway outlines, the band's gold edge, the formation strips. No pinstripes for their own sake.

transitions.how: Masked hard edges for every marking; soft only for heat round the exhausts and for grime.
